summary: Repeat-prompt latency spike and 504 timeouts traced to prefix/KV cache miss storm
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (WaveDocs, dedicated) report that repeated prompts which previously returned sub-200ms token latency are now observing 600-1200ms per-token latency and intermittent 504 timeouts. Behavior appears when clients send sequences with short prefixes repeated across requests (prefix caching expected to accelerate these).

Impact:
- WaveDocs: significant increase in API timeouts for interactive sessions; several user sessions dropped.
- Overall elevated 95th/99th latency for rw-7b model on prod us-east.

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1), Dedicated pool DW-72 (pinned to redwood-rw-7b-v1).
- Observed across multiple nodes; not isolated to single GPU instance.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start an interactive session with WaveDocs app (session ID provided).
2) Send initial prompt: "Summarize the document: <short prefix>" repeatedly with slight tail edits.
3) Observe first request fast, following repeat requests significantly slower and sometimes time out after 30s.

Observed behavior:
- First prompt typically returns under 200ms per token.
- Subsequent prompts that share prefix show large variance; many are in 600-1200ms per token or hit gateway 504s.
- Logs show high rate of cache misses for prefix/KV keys that should have been warm.

Expected behavior:
- Prefix/KV cache should produce cache hits for shared prefixes and reduce per-token compute latency to baseline (<250ms).

Relevant logs (excerpts):
- serving-runtime@node-7: [2026-03-12T09:14:22Z] prefix_cache: miss key="sess-abc:prefix-hash-0x7f3b"
- serving-runtime@node-12: [2026-03-12T09:14:23Z] kv_cache: put key="sess-abc:prefix-hash-0x7f3b", size=1.2MB
- scheduler: [2026-03-12T09:14:25Z] cache_eviction: evicted 28 keys from node-12, policy=LRU, low_mark=0.3
- api-gateway: [2026-03-12T09:14:55Z] request_id=R-91 timeout waiting for response (504)

Attachments: customer session traces, sample request/response bodies, flamegraph snippets (uploaded to ticket attachments).
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support + SRE 2026-03-12: reproduced increased miss rate on prefix cache for the WaveDocs workload. Observed symptoms:
- Cache hit rate for prefix/KV dropped from ~82% baseline to ~28% during incident window.
- Eviction events spiked concurrently with small, frequent writes to KV cache.
- Found a normalization regression introduced in runtime PR #1279 (key generation changed to include ephemeral session metadata).
- Regression causes identical logical prefixes to generate different cache keys across requests (session-scoped noise in key).
- Additionally, LRU low_mark tuning combined with larger-than-expected serialized KV values (some keys ~1.2MB) led to aggressive eviction to keep node memory under threshold.
- Race window: parallel requests occasionally write duplicate but slightly different keys, causing cache churn and underutilization.

Hypotheses tested:
- H1: Key normalization bug -> confirmed by reproducing mismatched key hashes across identical logical prefixes.
- H2: Eviction threshold too low for dedicated pool workload -> supported by eviction logs and memory profiles.
- H3: Large persisted key sizes amplify eviction -> validated; sample traces show many keys >1MB.

Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-12 15:40Z):
- Rolled forward config change to disable inclusion of ephemeral session metadata in prefix key (feature-flag rollback) on dedicated pool DS-72.
- Increased cache low_mark from 0.3 to 0.45 on affected nodes to reduce churn while we patch serialization.
- Enabled transient bypass for prefix caching on particularly noisy sessions (WaveDocs) as a stopgap to prevent 504s.

Current status: mitigation reduced 99th token latency by ~45% and eliminated timeouts for WaveDocs in the short window. Root-cause fix still required in serving-runtime.
workaround:
Applied workarounds in prod for WaveDocs:
- Feature-flag rollback to prior stable key normalization (removed ephemeral session metadata from cache key).
- Increased cache watermarks on dedicated pool nodes.
- Optional customer-side workaround: set session option "prefetch_kv=false" or include explicit cache_key parameter normalized by client.
These reduce immediate impact but are not durable fixes.
resolution_plan:
Short term (next 48h):
- Merge hotfix PR #1284 to normalize prefix cache key generation deterministically (no session noise).
- Add defensive deduplication in cache put path to collapse near-duplicate keys.
- Adjust low_mark defaults per-pool based on observed payload size distribution.
- Deploy hotfix canary to 10% of prod nodes (us-east) for 2h, run synthetic workload and WaveDocs test harness.

Long term (2-4 weeks):
- Revise KV serialization to compress large prefix blobs and introduce size limits per-key.
- Implement better cache metrics/alerts (delta-hit-rate threshold) and automated protective heuristics (backpressure before eviction storms).
- Postmortem and customer follow-up.

PR/changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1284 (hotfix), https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/605 (watermark tuning).
